intended_object: The canonical generator δ_i of the module ⊕_i R[X]/(X − a_i): the class of 1 in the i-th summand, with zeros elsewhere. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the lemma `pointSquareZeroDelta_annihilated`.
explanation: The body is `DirectSum.lof R[X] ι _ i (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ 1)`: the inclusion of the i-th summand R[X]/ker(eval at a_i) = R[X]/(X − a_i), applied to the class of 1. This is exactly the canonical coordinate the docstring describes. Degenerate cases cause no problem: with ι empty there is no index to choose, and with R the zero ring the summand is zero, which is still correct. The definition is already stated for an arbitrary commutative ring R and an arbitrary index type ι; `classical` only supplies the decidable equality on ι that `DirectSum.lof` needs. Mathlib has no separate named declaration for this specific element.
